parole.significato: A tongue or tract of land included between two rivers, especially that between the Ganges and the Yamuna
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian دوآب (do-âb) and Hindi दोआब (doāb), properly meaning "two waters".

Apparently first used widely in English in the late 1960s or early 1970s. From Persian فارسی (fârsi), meaning "relating to Fars", the Arabicized form of the name of the province of Pars (Early New Persian پَارْس (pārs)) which was adopted in Iran following the Arab conquest of Persia in the 7th centu

parole.significato: A kind of coarse cotton cloth.
parole.testo: From Persian [Term?] and Hindi गज़ी (gazī). Possibly connected to guz/gaz, the fabric having been made a guz in length.

parole.significato: A temporary shelter used by soldiers during the First World War.
